ops.title: Fix host-dependent PATH isolation in test_scaffold.py codex_ask tests
ops.description:
Two tests fail on any dev machine that has codex installed via Homebrew. Green in
CI (GitHub runners have no codex), red locally, so the whole repo-bootstrap suite
looks broken to anyone running it on their own box.

Reproduced on a pristine `git archive HEAD` tree, so it predates the Sept 2026
codex-ask hook-latency work (P0/P1/P2) and is unrelated to it.

    FAILED test_scaffold.py::test_codex_ask_await_failure_status_and_clean_errors
    FAILED test_scaffold.py::test_codex_ask_worker_spawn_failure_durable_status

    E  AssertionError: test PATH must resolve no real codex
    E  assert '/opt/homebrew/bin/codex' is None
    E   +  where '/opt/homebrew/bin/codex' = which('codex', path='/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin')

Diagnosis: both tests build their "bare" PATH from `os.path.dirname(shutil.which("uv"))`
so that uv stays reachable, then assert that PATH resolves no real `codex`. On a
machine where uv and codex are both Homebrew-installed, that dirname IS
/opt/homebrew/bin, which also holds codex — so the isolation assumption the
assertion guards is false and the test fails before it exercises any product code.

Fix direction: stop deriving the sandbox PATH from a sibling tool's location.
Either symlink just the uv binary into a tmp bindir and use that as the whole PATH,
or resolve uv by absolute path and drop it from PATH entirely. Both keep the
126/127 assertions meaningful without depending on what else the host has in brew.

ops.text: test_codex_ask_await_failure_status_and_clean_errors passes on a machine with a brew-installed codex on PATH
The tests still prove the 126/127 no-codex-on-PATH behaviour they were written to cover
